prompt:
Create a complete neutral rough monochrome film storyboard page on white paper: exactly 12 clearly separated panels arranged in 3 columns and 4 rows, read left to right and top to bottom. Each panel is a portrait 9:16 camera composition. Pencil/charcoal contour sketches only, unpolished production planning. Human silhouettes have ordinary simplified human head and torso proportions, NOT round-head stick figures, NOT whiteboard glyphs, NOT polished ChronoStick production art. No color, photorealism, final costume design, source logos or detailed face likeness. The wooden-boy puppet prop has a short nose, small cap and visible elbow/knee joints. Cinema/studio/dock equipment fits the early 1940s. No readable text inside the scenes. Put only the exact planning panel IDs in each panel margin. Every panel must depict its own composition, do not merge or omit panels. Maintain the same simple producer silhouette where he recurs.

S01: Close film-screen puppet. A jointed wooden boy with a short nose and small cap appears as a projected film image. No literal soldier puppet.
S02: Wide wartime horizon. A faraway European skyline beneath two tiny aircraft silhouettes; no casualties, no attack on the American cinema.
S03: Wide cinema exterior. A 1940 American cinema with blank marquee and one wooden-puppet poster without writing; no people.
S04: Wide cinema interior. Rows of mostly empty seats; exactly two adult silhouettes seated apart face a screen with a puppet image.
S05: Close projector. One projector reel rotates beside a beam; no person in this shot.
S06: Medium producer at studio. Exactly one suited male producer looks from a film reel toward a blank receipt on his desk.
S07: Medium dock delivery. Exactly one delivery worker carries one round film canister toward a port gate; ship shape far behind.
S08: Close dock gate. The same worker holds one film canister before a visibly closed barrier; symbolic lost distribution, no labels.
S09: Extreme close drawing pile. A plain human hand places a puppet drawing on a thick pile of animation drawings; only one visible hand.
S10: Over-shoulder animator. Exactly one animator bends over a drawing board with puppet sketches; no finished identity design.
S11: Close cash drawer. A plain human hand opens a cash drawer containing only two loose coins; no dollar symbol or numbers.
S12: Close producer reaction. Exactly one suited producer studies a blank bill, shoulders lowered; no second person.

This is internal composition planning for an approximately 30-second historical Short. Clear primary props, exact visible subject counts, one simple action per panel; no decorative additions.
